title: Ein Sof: God without end
hookLine: God as the Infinite, beyond any description
carry: ein sof: the one god beyond every word

lines: EVERY DRAWING STARTS WITH A LINE.
cards: How do you draw something with no edges? Every drawing starts with a line, and a line is a boundary: this is inside, that is outside. A word works the same way.
Call something kind, and you've drawn a line around it, kind and not cruel. Now try it with God. Every word you reach for draws a line.
Each one is true in its way, and each one is too small. Jewish mystics gave that problem a name, a name that is really a refusal to draw any line at all.

teach.b: Ein Sof. In Hebrew, ein means there is no, and sof means end. Without end.
Kabbalists use it for God as God is in God's own self, before and beyond any way of being known. First, it's hardly a name.

teach.h: A NAME THAT SAYS WHAT GOD IS NOT.
teach.b: A name usually tells you what something is. This one tells you only what it is not: not ending, not bounded, not measured.
After weeks with Maimonides, you'll hear a cousin of his teaching, that we speak more truly of God by saying what God is not. The kabbalists take that silence and give it a title.
Second, the Psalms point the same way. The psalmist praises God, then admits that God's greatness is beyond searching out. Praise, and then the edge of what praise can do.
Third, Ein Sof is not a second God hiding behind the first. Kabbalists insist that God is one.
Ein Sof is the one God from the side that can't be spoken of: not a different being, but the same One, seen from where every word runs out. Fourth, the turn.

teach.h: HOW DOES THE ENDLESS TOUCH THE WORLD?
teach.b: If God is without end, beyond every description, how does God touch a world with edges, a world of kitchens and buses and birthdays?
That question drives the whole system ahead, and the mystics answer it with lights. For today, just stand where they stood, at the edge of the drawing, looking at the space with no line around it.

how: In Kabbalah, Ein Sof is the term for God beyond all description; students usually meet it at the start of an introduction to the sefirot, as the one source from which everything else unfolds.

o: a second, hidden God behind the God of the Torah
God beyond every limit, name and description
the end of days, when the world will be complete

s: Ein Sof is a second God behind the God of the Torah
kabbalists insist God is one. Ein Sof speaks of the one God from the side that can't be described.
the name Ein Sof says what God is not
not ending, not bounded: a name built from a refusal to draw a line.
kabbalists say Ein Sof can be fully described with the right words
the whole point of the name is that every description is too small.

games.q: you've just said God is without end, beyond every description. a friend asks: then how does God touch a world of kitchens and buses?
o: God doesn't touch the world at all.
that's the question the mystics answer next, with lights.
God must have edges after all.
games.why: the kabbalists' whole system grows from this question. their answer comes as lights, the sefirot.

practice: Go to a window or step outside if you can, or close your eyes and remember the widest sky you've ever seen, and let your eyes rise past the roofs and wires and trees to where there's nothing to rest on.
When your gaze wants an edge, a cloud, a bird, let it keep going instead. If you pray, you can simply be quiet before the One without end.

wordCard.voice: Ein Sof. Without end: the kabbalists' way of speaking of God as God is in God's self, beyond every name and description. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: there is no end. The kabbalists' term for God beyond all description.

carryVoice: Your line: ein sof: the one god beyond every word. Every word for God draws a line; this name refuses to. That's today, done.
